title: SlatePay POC kickoff — QPS & concurrency projection
summary: Kickoff to scope a 6-week POC to validate SlatePay conversational fraud detection and reconciliation assistant. Main goals: map QPS/concurrency, define input/output token distributions, establish benchmark plan and success criteria covering latency, cost, and accuracy. Discussed hosted vs private deployment constraints (VPC/KMS), and initial sizing estimate ~120–180 peak QPS with burst to 400. Agreed next steps: provide benchmark plan and pilot pricing, run sample traffic replay, schedule infra readiness call.
topics: Traffic profile: QPS, concurrency, burst patterns
Token distribution: prompt vs response lengths
Deployment options: Hosted API vs Private VPC/Dedicated

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-13
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 56m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Evan (SlatePay Head of Platform), Priya (SRE), Marco (CTO), Jasmine (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): discuss workload shape and define POC success gates; record sample token distribution; sign off on pilot timeline.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through scope and try to leave with a clear plan for the pilot, um if we can, quick intros?
00:12 Evan: sure I'm Evan, head of platform at SlatePay, we own infra for the payments and reconciliation products
00:18 Jasmine: Jasmine, product, i'm owning acceptance criteria on our side
00:22 Priya: Priya, SRE, i'll be doing the infra work and the staging replay stuff
00:27 Marco: Marco, CTO, here to understand risk and deployment options
00:31 Jordan: great, maya are you on for the sizing bits?
00:34 Maya: yup will cover the QPS/concurrency mapping and the benchmark plan after we hear more about traffic shape
00:39 Speaker 2: okay perfect

01:05 Evan: to give context — this bot is used by our reconciliation ops and fraud ops teams; traffic is hybrid, about 80% short lookups and 20% longer conversation sessions. We expect peak in US business hours, everyday batch windows at midnight cause sweeps.
01:26 Jordan: okay do you have any ballpark QPS today or a t-shirt number?
01:31 Evan: currently internal tooling sits around 20 QPS on average but the expectation with productization and enablement is to hit steady 120 QPS and bursts up to 400 during promos or incidents
01:44 Priya: yeah and concurrency is weird because sessions can hold a KV cache for the duration — we'd expect concurrency for long-running sessions maybe 50–80 at peaks
01:54 Maya: when you say "sessions hold cache" — is that per user session with long context stored server-side?
01:59 Priya: yes we keep a partial KV cache for up to 15 minutes for in-flight reconciliation flows

03:10 Jordan: great that's actionable. let's map that to tokens. what's your typical prompt length and expected model response length?
03:16 Evan: median prompt today is small — 30–50 tokens for a query, but for guided reconciliation flows the prompts can be 120–250 tokens. Response lengths vary, median output about 140 tokens, 95th about 480 tokens for verbose diffs
03:34 Maya: ok so distribution is skewed — many short requests but heavy tail. for benchmarking we need percentiles: p50/p90/p95/p99 input and output token sizes, and separate the two traffic classes: quick lookups vs multi-step conversation.
03:50 Jasmine: we also need accuracy gating — it's not just latency for us. Any benchmark must include a small eval set for reconciliation correctness and false positive rate for fraud detection
04:02 Jordan: noted. success criteria draft — is everyone comfortable with an initial gate like: p95 latency under 350ms for short queries, p99 under 1.2s; for long sessions p95 under 900ms? we can tune after the first run
04:18 Marco: those numbers seem optimistic for large outputs — how much of that assumes Redwood's prefix/KV cache?
04:24 Maya: good call — our runtime will use KV caching and prefix reuse where sessions are repeated. the short lookups should benefit from cache hits and batching; long sessions will rely on continuous KV cache and potentially quantized model variants
04:36 Priya: we're going to need a private option; we have a compliance requirement to keep certain PII inside our VPC and use customer KMS for key management
04:44 Jordan: SlatePay's compliance ask makes sense. we can scope pilot on hosted with a shadow private pilot later, or start with Redwood Private (VPC) for the POC. tradeoffs are time to run benchmarks vs. extra infra build — private takes 2–3 weeks to stand up the control plane + network peering
04:59 Evan: timeline is tight. we'd prefer hosted for speed but must ensure logs and payloads exclude PII, otherwise private. how do you redact or keep telemetry minimal?
05:11 Maya: we can run a replay with token-level anonymization. for the POC you can run a synthetic generator that preserves token length distribution and timing. Jordan will share a CSV schema for the replay.
05:22 Jordan: yes i'll share schema and a sample script. we also need the sample of real logs if you can provide — anonymized.

06:30 Priya: about throughput — what's Redwood's recommended GPU mapping for mixed traffic with those token sizes?
06:35 Maya: initial estimate: for a generative model similar to M-size open model, at median 140 output tokens, we estimate roughly 8–10 RPS per GPU for latency SLO p95 ~400–800ms depending on batching. at 120 steady QPS you'd need around 12–15 GPU-equivalents capacity with continuous batching; but with aggressive batching and caching you can bring that down to ~8–10. bursts to 400 will need autoscale or burst pool.
06:57 Marco: can you translate that to instances or instance types? we use G* and A* families in cloud
07:02 Maya: we usually present capacity as GPU-equivalents; for G-class 80GB A100 you'd see different numbers; we'll provide a matrix mapping common cloud SKUs to expected RPS under the same profile in the sizing sheet.
07:14 Jordan: action: Maya builds candidate sizing for G- and A- class typical SKUs and shows cost delta between hosted and dedicated.

08:05 Evan: what about multi-tenant interference, noisy neighbors? if we go hosted do you have isolation guarantees?
08:12 Jordan: hosted has soft isolation w/ priority routing, but for strict isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private nodes — Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and clearer p99 guarantees. Hosted pilot is faster but less isolation.

09:30 Jasmine: we want cost per 1M tokens estimate for multiple scenarios — short vs long response mixes, and how KV caching affects costs
09:38 Maya: we'll produce cost-per-token modeling with and without KV cache; caching reduces effective output tokens when prefix reuse is high, but depends on cache hit rates — we should target a conservative 30% hit rate for initial planning and run sensitivity to 60%+ in best-case scenarios

11:10 Priya: for benchmarks, we want: load test with realistic concurrency distribution, latency percentiles, throughput plateau, and correctness eval. also a resilience test for network flaps and autoscale behavior
11:23 Jordan: yes recommended benchmark runs: 1) baseline steady-state (60–120 QPS) for 20–30 minutes; 2) burst ramp (up to 400) with step increases to see autoscale; 3) tail test of 99–100 percentile tokens to capture long outputs; 4) correctness eval on 250 sample dialogs.

13:00 Evan: who will run the replay? we prefer Redwood run in staging against our sandbox keys so we don't expose production keys
13:07 Maya: Redwood can run the replay inside a sandbox cluster but we need the anonymized traffic CSV and a staging endpoint; Redwood will need IAM role access and short-lived creds; Priya will coordinate

15:20 Marco: what's the expected pilot duration and gating for go/no-go to production?
15:25 Jordan: typical POC is 4–6 weeks: week 0–1: traffic collection and synthetic generator; week 2: first benchmark runs; week 3–4: tuning, accuracy evaluation and SLA negotiation; week 5–6: run production-like replay and finalize sizing/cost, then decision.
15:40 Jasmine: can we compress to 4 weeks? we have a launch window in mid-May
15:44 Priya: only if we accept hosted pilot and prioritize effort; private would add 2–3 weeks
15:49 Jordan: ok we'll propose a compressed 4-week track (hosted) and a conservative 6-week track (Private/Dedicated).

20:00 Speaker 3: slight crosstalk, speaker mislabeling

22:10 Evan: any security paperwork ahead of replay? we need NDA addendum and SOC 2 docs
22:16 Jordan: we'll share SOC 2, our compliance pack, and a DPA. can get them today/tomorrow.

28:40 Maya: for the replay CSV, fields: timestamp, conversation_id, input_tokens_est, output_tokens_est, timing_interarrival_ms, route_hint (quick_lookup|full_convo). will also include a column for label if you want to run correctness checks
28:55 Priya: we'll emit that from our logs with PII redaction and share a 7-day slice

33:20 Jasmine: on accuracy gates — what metric do you accept? precision/recall thresholds?
33:27 Maya: recommended: reconciliation accuracy >= 92% on sample set, fraud false positive rate <= 1.2% (or align to your baseline). we can tune prompt engineering and reranking; Redwood doesn't change model weights in this POC, but offers reranking and structured output guidance

39:02 Marco: what about model choices — open LLM vs a tuned closed LLM?
39:08 Jordan: we'll propose two model families: a medium open model we know latency/cost for, and a higher-quality variant (could be hosted proprietary or a larger open model). we'll include both in the benchmark matrix so you can assess cost/accuracy tradeoff

45:00 Evan: recap?
45:05 Jordan: recap — deliverables from Redwood: benchmark plan + replay schema (by Apr 17), sizing sheet with GPU mapping & cost projection (by Apr 19), compliance pack and DPA (tomorrow). Customer deliverables: provide anonymized traffic sample or confirm synthetic generator (by Apr 20), schedule infra deep dive with Priya. Aim to start pilot first week of May if hosted path chosen.
45:32 Priya: yep that's fine
45:36 Jasmine: agree on gating and timeline
46:10 Jordan: any other concerns?
46:18 Marco: just to note: if the 95th latency numbers stray, we'll need hard isolation for financial critical flows — that's a blocker to wide rollout
46:28 Jordan: understood, we'll make that a conditional decision in the SOW.

55:10 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule — i'll send meeting notes and next steps.
55:18 Evan: thanks all
55:20 End of call

Notes about transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker 2/3), small mis-hearings (K V cache written as K V cash), filler words preserved.
